newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds firm, Penn Traffic dips again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds firm, Penn Traffic dips again.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bond spreads were unchanged to Treasuries across all sectors on Monday, while high-yielding issues saw marginal gains, dealers said.

Penn Traffic Co resumed its slide in the debt market, however, with the 9-5/8 percent bonds off about four points on the day to 43 bid. The debt has fallen since early January when Wall Street analysts said Penn Traffic's same-store sales dropped 8.5 percent in December.
Dealers said the Penn Traffic bonds would continue to move in a wide range as holders scurry to reassess value.
"There are a lot of people who have been short these bonds and they're just starting to find fair value level," one trader said.

Other high-yield debt managed to eke out 1/8 point gains despite the anticipation of more than $5 billion in fresh supply slated over the next four to five weeks. Overall trade was moderate but dealers said activity would likely accelerate once new issues price.
Some large institutional accounts were busy positioning themselves ahead of new issues, a trader said.
One trader reported $26 million Tenet Healthcare 10-1/8 percent debt due 2005 traded in a tight 108 to 109 market ahead of a massive $1.3 billion three-part debt offering sometime in January.

Turning to high-grades, traders reported dull dealings which left prices with little impetus to deviate from current spreads to Treasuries. Bank and finance paper was little changed following strong but as expected fourth quarter earnings from NationsBank Corp and Barnett Banks.
Broadly speaking, traders characterized the Street as light and hungry for new issue paper, especially that with higher yield.
"It's quiet but there's a little bit of buying, perhaps more so than we've been seeing," a trader said. "Dealers have been buying up triple-Bs and waiting for new issues."

Among upcoming new issues, Philip Morris Cos Inc is expected to issue a $500 million 30-year debt offering via Merrill Lynch & Co at around 105 basis points over Treasuries, high-grade syndicate sources said on Monday.
